title: Review: Control of heart rate and ECGs; Sampling and investigating populations; Biodiversity and its measurement; Chi-squared test
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EC02#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV07a#t2 term and clue written for the game; EX08#t3 term and clue written for the game; EV07b#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EC02#N.4, EV07a#N.9b, EV07b#N.4a, EX08#N.10, IN06#N.11, EC02#N.14, EV07a#N.6b, EX08#N.14a, IN06#N.5a, EX08#N.7. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Random sampling
items.clue: Giving every point an equal chance of being chosen, which avoids bias

items.label: Species evenness
items.clue: How equally the individuals are spread among the kinds of organism present

items.label: Atrioventricular node
items.clue: Only route through the non-conducting layer; delays the wave by about 0.1 s

items.label: Alleles
items.clue: What members of one species differ in, although they all have the same genes

questions.stem: A student places ten 0.5 m × 0.5 m quadrats at random in a 250 m² meadow and counts 20 orchids in total. What is the estimated population of orchids in the meadow?

options.text: 2000 plants
20 plants
500 plants
20000 plants

questions.explanation: Each quadrat is 0.25 m², so the sampled area is 10 × 0.25 = 2.5 m². Density = 20 ÷ 2.5 = 8 orchids per m², and 8 × 250 m² = 2000 orchids.

questions.stem: Ecologists want to compare the species diversity of the plant communities in two meadows by calculating Simpson's Diversity Index for each. Which procedure is most appropriate?

options.text: List the different plant species found in each meadow, without counting the individuals of each.
Count the total number of plants in each meadow, without recording which species each belongs to.
Count the individuals of each species in several randomly placed quadrats of equal size in each meadow.
Count the individuals of each species in one quadrat placed in the middle of each meadow.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. In a rare breed of sheep, 40 gene loci were tested. 6 were polymorphic and 34 were monomorphic. What is the proportion of polymorphic gene loci?
questions.explanation: 6 ÷ 40 = 0.15. Low genetic diversity, typical of a small, closed breeding population.

questions.stem: A person stands up quickly and their blood pressure falls for a few seconds. Which sequence describes the feedback response that restores blood pressure?

options.text: Baroreceptors in the arteries send fewer impulses to the medulla, which sends sympathetic impulses that raise heart rate and stroke volume.
Baroreceptors detect the fall and the medulla sends impulses along the vagus nerve to reduce heart rate, because a lower rate lets the pressure recover.
The medulla sends the impulses that cause each heartbeat more frequently, because the heart cannot beat at all unless the medulla drives it.
Baroreceptors in the heart wall detect the fall in pressure and the heart raises its own rate without any involvement of the medulla.

questions.stem: In tomatoes, purple stems (A) are dominant to green stems (a). An Aa plant is crossed with an aa plant. Of 200 seedlings, 115 are purple and 85 are green (illustrative data). Critical values at p = 0.05: 3.84 for 1 degree of freedom, 5.99 for 2. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: χ² = 4.5; with two classes there are 2 degrees of freedom, so 4.5 < 5.99 and the difference is not significant.
χ² = 4.5, which is above 3.84, so the data fit the 1 : 1 ratio well.
χ² = 4.5, which is above 3.84, so the difference is significant: reject the null hypothesis of 1 : 1.
Reject the null hypothesis, because 115 and 85 are not exactly 100 each.

questions.stem: A student estimates the number of dandelions on a school field. She places ten quadrats in the spots where she can see dandelions growing, counts carefully, and scales up by the area of the field. Which statement about her estimate is correct?

options.text: It will be accurate, because she counted every dandelion in each quadrat carefully.
It will be exact if she places fifty quadrats the same way instead of ten.
It is likely to be too high, because the quadrats were not placed at random.
Choosing spots with dandelions is better than random placement, because it gives typical samples.

questions.explanation: She sampled only where dandelions grow, so her mean density is higher than the field's. Random coordinates give every point an equal chance.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. A rock pool holds limpets 8, barnacles 6, periwinkles 4 and sea anemones 2. Using D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², what is Simpson's Index of Diversity?
In a heart transplant, the nerves linking the donor heart to the medulla are cut, and they do not regrow for many months. Which statement about the transplanted heart is correct?

options.text: It cannot beat until the nerves regrow, because each beat needs an impulse from the brain.
It beats steadily, because its SAN starts each beat, but the medulla can no longer adjust its rate quickly.
Its rate still rises at once when blood pressure falls, because the baroreceptors are in the heart wall itself.
Its atria and ventricles now contract together, because nerves from the brain normally time the ventricles.

questions.stem: A student carries out a chi-squared test on the F2 offspring of a dihybrid cross. Which statement about the test is correct?

options.text: The null hypothesis is that observed and expected numbers do not differ significantly, and the F2 counted is a sample of the population
The null hypothesis is that the two genes are linked, so that the observed numbers will differ from those expected from the predicted ratio
If the calculated chi-squared value is below the critical value at p = 0.05, the null hypothesis has been proved to be true
The number of degrees of freedom equals the number of phenotype classes, so a cross that produces four classes has four degrees of freedom

questions.explanation: The null hypothesis states no difference beyond chance between observed and expected results. The F2 that was counted is a sample.

questions.stem: On an ECG recorded at 25 mm s⁻¹, the distance between two R peaks is 30 mm. What is the heart rate in beats per minute?
questions.explanation: R–R time = 30 ÷ 25 = 1.2 s. Rate = 60 ÷ 1.2 = 50 beats min⁻¹.
